event.summary: Check restored update-survival assurance against old-terminal retirement
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 78e9d68a95119db8452ee139efde13d38546f648. TLDR: the restored assurance that sessions keep running during an update may mislead someone whose old-terminal agents and background work this release deliberately ends. Source basis: assigned SPEC.md patch restores the unconditional assurance at 762–763 and 3459–3461; same-revision SPEC.md search locates the old-terminal ending at about 3005; commit message explicitly says the installer prints the assurance during the one migration too. Suggested bucket: highest if the reassurance induces updating with live work; could-be-highest: yes, processes/work may end, but the inducement route and specification acceptance need checking. Confidence: lead, not yet settled. proposed_drop: false pending complete governing retirement text and implementation check. possible_cover: the commit message explicitly accepts printing the general statement during the migration; no queue coverage searched. Next checks: read complete retirement bullet and corresponding implementation section at this revision; establish what warning the shipped flow provides and whether the exact reassurance is an explicitly accepted documentation omission. No execution performed.

event.summary: Blanket update-survival assurance includes the update that ends old terminals (proposed drop)
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 78e9d68a95119db8452ee139efde13d38546f648. TLDR: a reader is assured that sessions keep running when restarting to update, even during the one migration that ends old-terminal agents, tabs and their attributable background processes. Original consequence retained: a reader relying on this assurance can update while live work remains, ending processes and losing their in-memory work. Suggested bucket: highest (documentation assurance can lead to loss of running processes/work); could-be-highest: yes. Confidence: confirmed source inconsistency and destructive migration route; no runtime behavior observed, and actual reader reliance is conditional. Details: SPEC.md 762–763 removes the old-terminal exception from Restart to update; 3459–3461 restores 'only a host reboot takes sessions down'. scripts/install.sh 1287 adds 'Your sessions keep running.' The same revision's SPEC.md 3001–3016 explicitly says the first supervisor start ends the private tmux server and its running agents/tabs; old agents' attributable descendants are swept too. SPEC_impl.md 2784–2833 specifies the startup destruction; source old_terminals.rs 164–173 calls end_server, 224–232 calls terminate_process_within with TERM/KILL graces. Earlier warnings existed, but SPEC.md 2803–2812 says new warnings are no longer recorded and affected live agents receive notice after ending; lost old tabs alone receive none. proposed_drop: the exact omission is deliberate in the reviewed commit's stated decision, so independent drop check should assess it rather than treating this as an accidental regression. Exact commit-message basis: 'Every other update keeps sessions running, so the general statement comes back without the caveat, accepting that the installer prints it during that one update too.' Exact governing SPEC.md Terminal experience text at 3004–3007: 'This release ends them: the first time a host’s supervisor of this release starts, it ends that tmux server, and with it everything that still ran in an old terminal, without needing a tmux program.' (The original uses ASCII apostrophe in host's.) The specification explicitly accepts ending the old terminals, but does not independently state that the inaccurate assurance is acceptable; the commit decision supplies that narrower acceptance. possible_cover: that explicit reviewed-commit decision; no queue/filter/TODO/plan coverage searched. Caveats: this does not challenge the deliberate terminal retirement, request a new migration prompt, or claim terminal-host sessions are ended. Checks actually made: read mandatory assurance patch, full retirement bullet, notification paragraphs, complete implementation retirement section, installer/implementation change, and startup destruction implementation through the signalling call. Source-only; no reproductions or tests run.

event.detail: Reviewed commit: 61e632323dbc6b4a35ed27bf5b9833102ffd5a4e. TLDR: no user-visible terminal behavior changes when the obsolete comparison with tmux is removed. Considered whether deleting the compatibility rationale weakens the child's permanent terminal-settings contract. Source refutation: the assigned patch retains kernel default termios, VERASE=DEL, IUTF8, cols/rows and zero pixel sizes verbatim at SPEC.md 124–127; spawn.rs 371–404 still implements each setting. SPEC.md Change policy 497–end still states: 'The journal’s behavior and the child’s process setup are part of the contract too: a newer client relies on an older running host behaving as this document says.' The removed sentences only compare these settings with an old terminal. Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed by source, no execution. Caveat: review is limited to this SPEC patch; the other files in this broad prose commit are assigned elsewhere.
